issues.description: simulate_msd_one_round: the template constructs a Stim circuit with stim.Circuit(n_shots) (template msd.py uses the function parameter n_shots as the constructor argument), while the reference solution constructs the circuit with stim.Circuit() (no argument). This conflates the number of simulation shots with the circuit's qubit-count argument to stim.Circuit and will confuse students implementing simulate_msd_one_round (they may mistakenly reserve qubits equal to the number of shots or misunderstand Stim's constructor semantics).
issues.suggestedFix: In the template, construct the circuit with stim.Circuit() (no args) inside simulate_msd_one_round to avoid implying n_shots is a qubit count. Update the template line circ = stim.Circuit(n_shots) -> circ = stim.Circuit(). Add a short comment clarifying that n_shots is the number of simulation samples (shots) passed to the sampler, not the number of qubits in the circuit.
